t: XML Parser - Signature build-tool concept
title: XML Parser - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Extracts structured data from XML documents.
description:
Every build an AI undertakes passes through XML Parser: Extracts structured data from XML documents. The catalog lists it among the thousand fundamental build tools because no serious building happens without it. This database is its Signature edition - the concept rebuilt as a deterministic framework with seven pillars, grounded in real techniques and standards, and taught through a ladder of runnable drills.

The Signature line treats XML Parser as infrastructure, not inspiration. Infrastructure has contracts: given these inputs, in this state, the XML Parser produces that output, and anyone can verify it. The seven pillars are those contracts made concrete - each owns one responsibility, each can be tested alone, and together they compose into the full capability. The technique records show the real public knowledge the pillars stand on.

Work through this database the way you would commission a machine: read the charter in the overview, inspect each pillar, check the techniques against your own knowledge, then run the drills. Every record includes a program you can execute with node - the XML Parser is demonstrated, not merely described.

t: Signature Harvester - XML Parser framework pillar
title: Signature Harvester - XML Parser framework pillar
definition: The Harvester component of the Signature XML Parser framework, owning harvester. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature XML Parser framework decomposes the capability (Extracts structured data from XML documents.) into seven pillars, and the Harvester is the one that owns the framework's harvester responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a XML Parser result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Harvester's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Harvester's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for XML Parser. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Listener - XML Parser framework pillar
title: Signature Listener - XML Parser framework pillar
definition: The Listener component of the Signature XML Parser framework, owning listener. Signature concept.
description:
The Listener is a load-bearing component of the Signature XML Parser framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's listener responsibilities belongs to the Listener, and the Listener answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Listener can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Listener works like this. A build request arrives carrying the XML Parser charter (extracts structured data from XML documents.). The Listener reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for an small ingestion job that needs XML Parser. The Listener takes the request's listener responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Listener's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for XML Parser. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Tapper - XML Parser framework pillar
title: Signature Tapper - XML Parser framework pillar
definition: The Tapper component of the Signature XML Parser framework, owning tapper. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature XML Parser framework, the Tapper owns the framework's tapper responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Tapper's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Tapper from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Extracts structured data from XML documents.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Data collection and ingestion build needs XML Parser, so the framework invokes the Tapper on the the framework's tapper responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.
